name: Multiculturalism
summary: Multiculturalism holds that a state should recognise and accommodate its cultural, ethnic, linguistic and religious diversity rather than require minorities to assimilate. It combines equal citizenship with group-sensitive measures such as language support, religious accommodation and, for national minorities and indigenous peoples, self-government. Critics argue it undermines cohesion, national identity or gender equality; adherents dispute this.
scope: Liberal multiculturalism as a public philosophy and policy in Western democracies, based on Canadian official policy (the Multiculturalism Act), Will Kymlicka, Charles Taylor and Bhikhu Parekh. It excludes the descriptive sense of mere demographic diversity and radical identity-politics variants, and says little on economic questions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Multiculturalism arose as a rejection of assimilation ideals, holding that immigrants may keep their cultural identity while integrating.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Multiculturalism treats cultural plurality within one state as normal and valuable, the opposite of a mono-ethnic national ideal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Canadian Act pairs recognition of diversity with equal treatment and equal protection under the law for all individuals.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Supporters link multiculturalism to removing barriers that kept minorities from full equality, and the Act promotes removing barriers to participation.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Adherents see the national culture as plural and evolving, and reject privileging one culture; critics say it weakens host culture.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Supporters see immigration as socially and economically valuable, with Canada as the model.

open-borders.rationale: Multiculturalism supports immigration and fair integration but is mostly a theory about managing diversity within borders, not about abolishing borders.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Self-government claims are strongest for indigenous peoples and national minorities in the Kymlicka account.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from concern with equal respect and hate speech by politicians as a cohesion risk, though the SEP entry does not address speech directly.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Kymlicka defends group-differentiated rights; Barry, a critic, rejects them as incompatible with universalist liberalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Defenders argue diversity does not itself undermine cohesion and cite cross-national evidence of no systematic trade-off.

elite-replacement.rationale: Multiculturalists see immigration as legitimate policy; the replacement claim is a critic narrative, not a multicultural position.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Taylor presumes the equal worth of cultures and Parekh argues justice must emerge from dialogue among cultures, though not every adherent denies all comparison.

universal-morality.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists keep universal liberal values as a starting point while Parekh says no framework is impartial; adherents are split.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Parekh and Kymlicka deny state cultural neutrality, but this is not a claim about knowledge in general.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious exemptions from general laws and accommodation are central, so uniform treatment regardless of religion is resisted.

more-religion-public.rationale: Adherents defend religious accommodation and toleration but do not generally want religion to play a larger role.

separate-church-state.rationale: Accommodating religious practice is central, but adherents mostly accept liberal secular states; split on strictness.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Liberal multiculturalists often favor secular schools while some accommodate faith schools; split.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from the Act and liberal premises on freedom of conscience and religion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: religious-based bans imposed on all would conflict with equal treatment of diverse practices.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Multiculturalism promotes equal treatment and removal of racial barriers, directly opposing legal segregation.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposed by the commitment to equal worth and to removing barriers to participation of all origins.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from anti-racism and equal worth of cultures and peoples as central premises.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to equal treatment and protection of all individuals.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring minorities to leave contradicts protecting minority communities and their historic contributions.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the focus on equitable participation of immigrants; adherents are not unanimous.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on inclusion and full participation of immigrants.

national-self-determination.rationale: Self-government is defended for national minorities such as Quebec, though not an independent-state claim.

revive-national-language.rationale: Policies support minority and indigenous languages, e.g. Bolivia and Canada, so revival is broadly favored.

right-to-secede.rationale: Quebec-style autonomy is defended but adherents are split on secession.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from equal-respect liberalism, though some minority communities object.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist multiculturalists stress gender subordination within groups; inferred for society generally.

harm-principle.rationale: Kymlicka rejects internal restrictions and defends external protections, a liberal harm-style limit.

democracy-best.rationale: Liberal democracy is the setting of the theory.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred from the liberal democratic framework.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred as favoring minority representation; not a stated doctrine.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a multicultural question; inferred from the left-liberal lean of most adherents and the equality aim.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Recognition and redistribution are both held necessary, but no stance on priority to the poor.

positive-liberty.rationale: Kymlicka justifies group rights by disadvantages that undermine real choice, close to a material view of freedom.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality is valued but religious communities seek accommodation; adherents split.

one-party-rule.rationale: Inferred as illiberal or exclusionary, at odds with the liberal-democratic, pluralist setting of multiculturalism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Kymlicka defends group rights but rejects internal restrictions that deny members basic liberties, including exit.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred: monetary union is not a multicultural issue and adherents hold no common view.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the Act's equality and participation goals in the country where people live.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from its openness to immigration and cross-cultural exchange.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from its equality-based approach that favours rights protections within trade.

moral-incentives.rationale: The scope excludes economic questions and no source states a position.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic, peaceful reform approach.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the Act's principle of equal treatment regardless of origin.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Multicultural policy favours curricula and public culture that recognise all of a society's heritages rather than centring one; inferred from the Act's heritage and understanding provisions.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Multiculturalism rests on equal respect for cultures and rejects ranking societies as more or less advanced, which is the premise of tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Adherents are split: Kymlicka-style liberals support civic nation-building, while others stress plural identities; the sources do not settle schooling.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Adherents generally accept group-sensitive measures such as employment equity to widen opportunity; inferred from the equal-participation aims, not stated on admissions.

public-money-creation.rationale: Multiculturalism is about cultural diversity and has no position on monetary arrangements.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The ideology is silent on economic crises; inferred indifference.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Multiculturalism's critique of colonial hierarchy suggests scepticism of claims to influence from past imperial rule; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Immigration and cultural exchange are welcomed, so economic delinking sits poorly with it; inferred, not an economic doctrine.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Multiculturalism treats minorities and workers as sharing equal citizenship and has no theory of a privileged rich-country working class; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Act commits government to equal treatment and non-discrimination, and adherents support anti-discrimination law over a right to refuse service.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism protects minority rights through entrenched constitutional guarantees such as the Canadian Charter, which the Act itself invokes.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed by the philosophy; inferred from the emphasis on self-government for national minorities and indigenous peoples.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; multiculturalism is compatible with either system.

minority-veto.rationale: Kymlicka-style liberal multiculturalism protects minority groups but through rights, not individual vetoes; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism values respect for others; inferred, not a stated position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Multiculturalism asks for public participation of minorities; inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Says little on economic questions, as the scope notes.

native-born-offices.rationale: Equal citizenship is a core principle, so reserving offices for the native-born contradicts it.

party-own-road.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not a position of multiculturalism; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Kymlicka argues for self-government rights of national minorities and indigenous peoples, though not a rule of leadership over settlers' descendants.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism emerges from post-war rejection of racial supremacism; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Adherents accept the scholarly view; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Adherents are split between preserving history and respecting minorities' objections.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Equal attention for disadvantaged groups follows from equal citizenship; inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Equal protection follows from equal citizenship, though critics say multiculturalism ignores gender; inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Multiculturalism holds that societies can have different forms of life, and each culture has equal worth, which includes different institutions, though this is about internal diversity.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism is a civilian, democratic doctrine; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not a stated position of this ideology and adherents are not clearly united; left neutral as an inference.

filial-duty.rationale: Multiculturalism takes no stand on family obligations; it only protects minorities' right to keep such norms.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; inferred only that it favours fair representation in public service, which is neither for nor against examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not a multicultural issue; the ideology says little on economic questions per its scope.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the liberal basis of equal citizenship and individual autonomy within groups, which the SEP discusses against illiberal practices.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology has no position on mandate and recall.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is silent on pension design.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; indigenous land claims are part of the debate but do not imply a general use-based tenure rule.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from its setting in liberal democracies where parliamentary control of spending is assumed.

single-official-language.rationale: Multiculturalism supports minority-language rights and rejects imposing one language on public life, as in the Canadian Act's language provisions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; no multicultural position on property rights of foreigners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from its attention to structural disadvantage of minorities, though liberal multiculturalists differ on how far outcomes count.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology says little on economic and lifestyle questions.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its liberal, rights-based internationalism, which does not endorse covert warfare, though it takes no direct position.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from respect for self-government of peoples and national minorities, which opposes forcible intervention to stop a state leaving a bloc.

corporate-influence.rationale: The liberal multiculturalism described here is mainly about cultural recognition and says little on lobbying, so this is a neutral inference.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred: multiculturalism supports civil-society, community and ethnic organisations, so limits on foreign funding of NGOs run against its openness.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: multiculturalism treats immigration as a normal, accepted source of population and diversity rather than something to offset.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from its equal-citizenship and anti-exclusion stance, which sits poorly with residency-based barriers that fall mostly on newcomers.

job-guarantee.rationale: The scope says little on economic questions, so there is no stated position.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; liberal multiculturalists are generally liberal-democratic but the idea is not part of the doctrine.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: liberal multiculturalism works within the rule of law and equal citizenship, though it accepts accommodation and exemptions for conscience.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed by the theory; adherents hold varied foreign-policy views.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic organisation is outside the scope of the ideology.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Multiculturalism Act commits to equal treatment of all cultural communities, which rejects casting a minority as a hostile conspiracy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: liberal multiculturalism relies on state-recognised equal citizenship and accommodation of religious family law practices, not abolishing legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from its liberal-democratic setting, where open government supports equal participation by minorities.

local-production.rationale: Economic localism is outside the scope of the ideology.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: it works through formal policy, institutions and group rights rather than informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred: Kymlicka and Parekh ground minority rights partly in international human-rights norms, so it does not put national law above them.

religious-nation.rationale: It treats a plural, multi-faith society as the goal and equal status for all religions, which rejects a nation defined by one religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A domestic-diversity doctrine that says nothing on interstate ritual; inferred from its equal-respect principle, which favours formal equality between states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Kymlicka-style liberal multiculturalism pairs minority self-government with civic solidarity, which favours some sharing across regions.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: liberal multiculturalism sits within market democracies and does not endorse common ownership of productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal-democratic commitments, with a coexistence stance more likely than a crusade.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the policy is about public institutions serving diverse communities, which is compatible with varied providers such as faith-based or community ones.

religion-illusion.rationale: Multiculturalism treats religion as a legitimate identity to be accommodated, so it rejects the view that religion is mere illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: the liberal-democratic strand is built on capitalist market economies and says little against them.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Liberal multiculturalism pursues equality through rights and accommodation, not economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: it stresses family and community autonomy in cultural practice, not public takeover of domestic work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Act supports heritage languages alongside the official ones, and pluralism treats language borrowing and mixing as normal.

treaties-binding.rationale: SEP discusses indigenous and national-minority rights, which adherents ground partly in treaties and agreements; inferred for the general principle.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: it keeps the existing state and market order and seeks diversity within it, not communal reorganisation.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-steered settlement to dilute minority regions is the kind of assimilationist nation-building multiculturalism opposes.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: the liberal strand works within capitalist democracy and has no third-way economic programme.

missingStatements.text: Governments should support minority languages in schools, public services and elections.
missingStatements.rationale: Language accommodation is a defining multicultural policy and is written into the Canadian Act.

missingStatements.text: Members of religious minorities should be exempt from general laws that burden their religious practice.
missingStatements.rationale: Religious exemptions are described as central to multicultural policy, though contested by Barry.

notes: Liberal multiculturalists (Kymlicka) reject internal restrictions; Taylor and Parekh are more communitarian or dialogical. Most economic and institutional answers are inferences.
